Utility functions

```{r}
# Function to align CDR3 AA sequences to IMGT, from https://github.com/immunogenomics/cdr3-QTL
all_imgt_pos <- c(
    "P104","P105","P106","P107","P108","P109","P110","P111",
    "P111.1","P112.2","P112.1",
    "P112","P113","P114","P115","P116","P117","P118")
align_imgt <- function(CDR3){
    AA <- unlist(strsplit(CDR3, ""));
    N_AA_fow <- nchar(CDR3) %/% 2 + nchar(CDR3) %% 2;
    N_AA_na <- 18 - nchar(CDR3);
    AAmod <- c(
        AA[1:(N_AA_fow)],
        rep("NA",N_AA_na),
        AA[(N_AA_fow + 1):nchar(CDR3)]
    );
    names(AAmod) <- all_imgt_pos
    return(t(AAmod))
}
```

## Calculating Normalized Mutual Information

Here we calculate the normalized mutual information (NMI) between two positions in the cdr3 sequence, for all possible positions. Each sequence length is (e.g. 15 aa.) is calculated at one at a time. We calculate normalized mutual information using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{MI} &= \sum_{i,j} P_{ij} \log \left( \frac{P_{ij}}{P_{i\cdot} P_{\cdot j}} \right) \\\\
H_x &= - \sum_i P_{i\cdot} \log P_{i\cdot} \\\\
H_y &= - \sum_j P_{\cdot j} \log P_{\cdot j} \\\\
\text{NMI} &= \frac{2 \cdot \text{MI}}{H_x + H_y}
\end{aligned}
$$



```{r}
# takes in a data frame with two columns named X and Y
# returns a data frame with the mutual information, Hx, Hy, and NMI
quantify_nmi <- function(df) {
    # make frequency table
    freq <- table(df[, 1], df[, 2])
    MI <- entropy::mi.empirical(freq, unit = c("log"))
    Hx <- entropy::entropy.empirical(colSums(freq))
    Hy <- entropy::entropy.empirical(rowSums(freq))
    NMI <- 2 * MI / (Hx + Hy) # normalized mutual entropy
    dump <- data.frame(MI, Hx, Hy, NMI)
    return(dump)
}

trust4_reports_tcrb_pid %>% glimpse()

# includes V, J, and CDR3aa
for (cdr3_len in 12:18) {
    print(paste0("Calculating for cdr3 length: ", cdr3_len))

    # prepare matrix
    filtered_df <- trust4_reports_tcrb_pid %>%
        filter(CDR3aa_len == cdr3_len)
    vjaa_df <- filtered_df %>%
        dplyr::select(V, J, CDR3aa)
    mat <- filtered_df %>%
        pull(CDR3aa) %>%
        as.character() %>%
        sapply(., function(x) {
            x <- as.character(x)
            x <- strsplit(x, "")
            x <- unlist(x)
        }) %>% 
        t() %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        rownames_to_column(var = "CDR3aa") %>%
        left_join(vjaa_df, by = "CDR3aa") %>%
        select(-CDR3aa) %>%
        glimpse()
    
    # name columns with IMGT positions - by default it fills colnames with IMGT positions - if shorter than 18 it will fill with NA
    imgt_vec <- align_imgt(filtered_df$CDR3aa[1])
    imgt_pos <- imgt_vec[,!imgt_vec[1,]=="NA"] %>% names() # drop NA columns to get IMGT positions
    default_names <- colnames(mat) %>% purrr::discard(. %in% c("V", "J"))
    colname_map <- stats::setNames(default_names, imgt_pos)
    mat %<>% dplyr::rename(!!!colname_map) %>%
        glimpse()

    res <- expand.grid(colnames(mat), colnames(mat)) %>%
        dplyr::rename(i = Var1, k = Var2) %>%
        mutate(res = furrr::future_map2(i, k, ~ quantify_nmi(mat[, c(.x, .y)]))) %>%
        unnest(res) %>%
        glimpse()

    saveRDS(res, glue("{entropy_dir}/cdr3_entropy_res_k{cdr3_len}_nmi_{Sys.Date()}.rds"))
}
```

Visualizing normalized mutual information

```{r}
mi_res <- list.files(entropy_dir, full.names = TRUE, pattern = "2025-08-14") %>%
    purrr::set_names(basename(.) %>% str_before_nth("_", -2)) %>%
    purrr::map(readRDS) %>%
    glimpse()
names(mi_res)

# list of antigen contact positions
antigen_contact_pos <- c(107:116, 111.1, 112.1, 112.2)  %>% paste0("P", .)

# Create pretty axis labels with red/bold for antigen contact positions
make_axis_labels <- function(levels, highlight_vec) {
  sapply(levels, function(lvl) {
    if (lvl %in% highlight_vec) {
      # Red and bold
    #   sprintf("<b style='color:#d62728;'>%s</b>", lvl)
      sprintf("<b style='color:#9f9fff;'>%s</b>", lvl)
    } else {
      lvl
    }
  })
}


for (cdr3_len in 12:18) {
    plot_df <- mi_res[[glue("cdr3_entropy_res_k{cdr3_len}")]] %>%
        glimpse()

    all_levels <- levels(plot_df$i)
    cdr3_pos_rank <- c(
        "V gene", all_levels[str_detect(all_levels, "^P")], "J gene"
    )
    axis_labels <- make_axis_labels(cdr3_pos_rank, antigen_contact_pos)
    names(axis_labels) <- cdr3_pos_rank

    p_nmi <- plot_df %>%
        mutate(i = case_when(
            i == "V" ~ "V gene",
            i == "J" ~ "J gene",
            TRUE ~ i
        )) %>%
        mutate(k = case_when(
            k == "V" ~ "V gene",
            k == "J" ~ "J gene",
            TRUE ~ k
        )) %>%
        mutate(i = factor(i, levels = cdr3_pos_rank)) %>%
        mutate(k = factor(k, levels = cdr3_pos_rank)) %>%
        ggplot(aes(x = i, y = k, fill = NMI)) +
        geom_tile() +
        scale_fill_scico(palette = "davos", direction = -1) +
        scale_x_discrete(labels = axis_labels) +
        scale_y_discrete(labels = axis_labels) +
        coord_fixed() +
        labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Normalized\nMutual\nInformation", title = paste0("CDR3aa Length = ", cdr3_len)) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(
            axis.text.x = ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
            axis.text.y = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 10),
            panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray90"),
            # panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
        )

    ggsave(
        glue("{entropy_plots_dir}/cdr3_entropy_heatmap_k{cdr3_len}_nmi.png"),
        p_nmi,
        width = 6,
        height = 6
    )
}
```

## **Conclusions:**

- We are able to reproduce the results from (Ishigaki et al., 2022).

- We calculated the normalized mutual information (NMI) between two positions in the cdr3 sequence, for all possible positions. Each sequence length is (e.g. 15 aa.) is calculated at one at a time.

- We see that the NMI is generally lower and entropy is higher for the antigen contact positions. 

- Positions (109-112) show very high entropy. These positions are generated via random recombination in the thymus.

- Flanking regions (104-108 & 113-118)  are almost completely defined by germline V or J genes, respectively, and thus share pairwise structure with V and J gene identity.
